title: Cancer Therapy Mechanisms and Evidence: A Cross-Literature Synthesis
description: Open-source cancer research consolidating the cancer-therapy literature into a single evidence-led synthesis: a CENSUS of the indexed cancer literature -- 5,187,265 articles, being 4,403,994 carrying MeSH indexing and 783,271 recovered by text match, with 10,509,470 typed entity relations -- measured with expert-assigned MeSH descriptors and NLM publication types rather than the project's own retrieval, so every prevalence claim is made over articles the project did not select. Paired with multi-scale computational simulations used to validate or disprove specific mechanistic claims across NINE selectable treatment arms -- ferroptosis induction, photodynamic and sonodynamic therapy, ionizing radiation, checkpoint blockade, adoptive cell therapy, oncolytic virus, thermal and electrical ablation, and antibody-drug conjugates -- alongside immune coupling, stromal shielding, drug penetration and tumor-microenvironment effects. The arms are NOT equally developed and the repository measures the difference rather than asserting parity: the ferroptosis and physical-ROS work carries the calibrated legs and every number the manuscript reports, while the other arms are roughly 11 to 13 times smaller by line count and are each recorded as feeding no reported number. Content classes and rights: (1) Code -- Python pipeline, Rust simulation engine, tests: MIT licensed. (2) Manuscript and analysis -- authored by the depositor, released under the repo MIT license. (3) Census metadata -- PMIDs, MeSH descriptors, publication types and typed relations; factual metadata is not copyrightable. (4) Abstracts -- non-copyrightable factual summaries (Feist v. Rural, 1991). (5) An earlier keyword-retrieved index, superseded by the census and retained only so published figures computed from it stay reproducible; no figure in this deposit rests on it. Excluded from this deposit: full-text articles, reference textbooks (Git LFS, CC BY 4.0 but 1.6 GB), and news articles (fair use, not a redistributable license). See PROVENANCE.yaml for full asset licensing details.
